newsitem.title: USA: UPS, Teamsters recess talks for 12 hours.
newsitem.headline: UPS, Teamsters recess talks for 12 hours.

text.p: The Teamsters union and United Parcel Service have recessed negotiations aimed at ending a two-week strike against the nation's largest package delivery company until noon EDT (1600 GMT) on Monday.
"The talks have recessed until noon," union spokesman Matt Witt told reporters shortly after midnight EDT (0400 GMT) on Monday. A Labor Department spokesman issued a similar statement.

Negotiators met at a downtown Washington hotel almost around-the-clock for four days at the request of Labor Secretary Alexis Herman. Teamsters President Ron Carey said Sunday that there had been some progress.

But he said reports that a settlement was near were inaccurate. President Bill Clinton told reporters on Sunday he had "a gut feeling" the two sides would reach a deal and, holding up two fingers not very far apart, added: "They're that close."

A Labor Department spokesman said Herman had canceled a trip to Los Angeles planned for on Monday in order to to remain closet at hand for consultations. She also canceled several scheduled television interviews on Monday morning.

The Aug. 4 walkout by 185,000 drivers, loaders and sorters crippled the nation's largest package delivery firm, costing it an estimated $300 million a week in lost revenues and hurting businesses that rely on it to ship their products.
